# State vector specification

*Generated by `python -m src.environment.observation` -- do not edit by hand.*

The observation is a `float32` vector of **58** entries: 14 global features describing the decision, followed by 11 features for each of the 4 devices.

Its width does not depend on the number of layers, so one policy places DNNs of any depth.

## Global block

| # | Feature | Meaning | Normalisation |
|--:|---|---|---|
| 0 | `progress_fraction` | Index of the layer being placed | divided by the DNN depth |
| 1 | `remaining_fraction` | Layers still to place, including this one | divided by the DNN depth |
| 2 | `inverse_depth` | Cue for how deep the DNN is | 1 / depth |
| 3 | `layer_compute_rel` | Compute cost of the current layer | divided by the mean layer compute cost of this DNN |
| 4 | `layer_memory_rel` | Memory footprint of the current layer | divided by the mean layer memory of this DNN |
| 5 | `layer_output_rel` | Activation this layer will emit | divided by the mean activation size of this DNN |
| 6 | `next_layer_compute_rel` | One-step lookahead: compute of the next layer | as above; zero on the final layer |
| 7 | `next_layer_memory_rel` | One-step lookahead: memory of the next layer | as above; zero on the final layer |
| 8 | `next_layer_output_rel` | One-step lookahead: activation of the next layer | as above; zero on the final layer |
| 9 | `remaining_compute_fraction` | Compute still to be placed | fraction of the DNN's total compute |
| 10 | `remaining_output_fraction` | Activation volume still to be produced | fraction of the DNN's total activation volume |
| 11 | `weight_alpha` | Latency weight of the objective | already in [0, 1] |
| 12 | `weight_beta` | Energy weight of the objective | already in [0, 1] |
| 13 | `weight_gamma` | Communication weight of the objective | already in [0, 1] |

## Per-device block

Repeated once per device, in action-index order: `edge_device`, `edge_server`, `gpu_server`, `cloud_server`.

| Offset | Feature | Meaning | Normalisation |
|--:|---|---|---|
| 0 | `effective_speed_rel` | Compute the device can currently deliver, after background and accumulated load | divided by the mean configured device capacity |
| 1 | `free_memory_ratio` | Memory still free on the device | fraction of that device's total memory |
| 2 | `utilisation` | Current load of the device | already in [0, 1] |
| 3 | `energy_per_compute_rel` | Energy cost of running work here | divided by the mean configured energy rate |
| 4 | `is_previous_device` | Whether the previous layer's activation already sits here | 0 or 1 |
| 5 | `link_latency_rel` | Latency of the link carrying the pending transfer | divided by the mean configured link latency; **fixed** reference, so congestion is visible |
| 6 | `link_bandwidth_rel` | Bandwidth of that link | divided by the mean configured link bandwidth; fixed reference |
| 7 | `is_feasible` | Whether this device can host the current layer | 0 or 1; mirrors the action mask |
| 8 | `estimated_execution_rel` | Execution time of the current layer here | divided by the scenario's latency reference per layer |
| 9 | `estimated_communication_rel` | Time to move the pending activation here | as above |
| 10 | `estimated_immediate_cost` | Weighted objective contribution of choosing this device now | multiplied by the depth, so it is around 1 for a typical decision |

## Notes

* **Layer features** are normalised by this scenario's own means, so they describe the
  *shape* of the workload and transfer across DNN depths.
* **Device and link features** are normalised by configuration midpoints, which are the
  same in every scenario. This is deliberate: normalising per scenario would rescale
  every link equally during a network-wide congestion event and hide it from the agent.
* **`estimated_immediate_cost`** is exactly the quantity the objective-aware greedy
  heuristic minimises. Giving it to the learning agent means the comparison measures
  decision quality rather than information asymmetry: any advantage the agent shows must
  come from looking beyond the current layer.
* The full ordered list of entry names is produced by `feature_names()` in
  `src/environment/observation.py`.
